record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Suppose f: [0,1]^2 -> R has all vertical sections f^x = f(x,·) continuous and all horizontal sections f_y = f(·,y) of the first Baire class. Must f be a pointwise limit of a sequence of separately continuous functions f_n: [0,1]^2 -> R?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.5. Does every function f : [0, 1]2 → R for which all vertical sections fx = f(x, ·) are continuous and all horizontal sections fy = f(·, y) belong to the first Baire class is a point-wise limit of a sequence of separately continuous functions fn : [0, 1]2 → R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:[0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function such that:

(i) for every $x \in [0,1]$, the vertical section $f^x : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, $y \mapsto f(x,y)$, is continuous;

(ii) for every $y \in [0,1]$, the horizontal section $f_y : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x,y)$, belongs to the first Baire class (i.e., is a pointwise limit of a sequence of continuous functions $[0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$).

A function $g:[0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be separately continuous if all its vertical sections and all its horizontal sections are continuous.

Question: Must every such $f$ be the pointwise limit of a sequence $\{f_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of separately continuous functions $f_n : [0,1]^2 \to \mathbb{R}$?
artifact.category_tag: Separately continuous functions and Baire classes
artifact.status_search_result: A web search on pointwise limits of separately continuous functions and Baire-class characterizations of sections turned up related work (e.g., Vallin's study of pointwise limits of separately continuous functions in Real Analysis Exchange) but no source explicitly resolving this specific question for functions on the unit square with continuous vertical sections and Baire-1 horizontal sections. The current status could not be confirmed from the search.

status_evidence.title: The Pointwise Limit of Separately Continuous Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates pointwise limits of separately continuous functions and their place in the space of Baire Class 2 functions, but does not explicitly address the stated question.
status_evidence.claim: Related but not a confirmed resolution of the problem.

status_evidence.title: Measurability of functions with approximately continuous vertical sections and measurable horizontal sections
status_evidence.snippet: Studies functions whose sections in one direction are approximately continuous and in the other direction satisfy a weaker regularity, related context but a different question.
status_evidence.claim: Related context on sectional regularity, not a resolution.
